sections.title: Habitat and form
sections.text: Watercress is a glabrous plant of springs, streams and freshwater ditches. Its floating or creeping stems are about 10–110 cm long, sometimes reaching 2 m.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The pinnate leaves usually have 3–9 leaflets, sometimes more, with a larger terminal leaflet. The small white flowers have four petals; the siliques are about 1–1.8 cm long.

sections.title: Edibility and hygiene
sections.text: The leaves and shoots are eaten raw or cooked and have a peppery flavour. Raw wild watercress can transmit liver flukes if contaminated; use a controlled supply or cook it, and avoid harvesting from risky water.
